doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: Would he have been ready for Bill Evans at 21; self-editing
summary: Joe doubts he could have handled Evans at 21 and talks about musicians' constant self-criticism.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: If my math is correct there was only about seven years between Woody Herman and Bill Evans. Is that correct?
Do you think you could have handled the gig with Bill Evans if you were 21, like when you joined Woody Herman?

I don’t think so, but I don’t know. I don’t know the answer to that. Honestly there are days when I think that I might just now be qualified to take that gig with Bill, honestly man. I mean you go through all of this, all of these periods of growth and self- examination and self-editing and all of, a lot of other things. But fortunately it came at a time I think when I’d had enough experience under my belt to be able to walk in there feeling confident that I could do the job.

What we play as musicians, you know, we’re the most self-critical people there are. We’re listening to ourselves play and if you’re doing a recording and you’re hearing the recording played back you say to yourself, “Oh man I’ve played that idea so many times, I’ve got to get that out of my vocabulary. That’s done for now.” Things like that, you know? Or if you find an obvious flaw in what you’re doing. You’re constantly examining yourself.
